Calculate locally

Use TypeScript or JavaScript for tropical charts, transits, and synastry in your own browser or Node.js app. Core calculations make no network requests.

Available · public files

Fetch shared sky data

Read the daily sky and dated events as JSON. No account or API key; check the edition and snapshot before displaying them.

Available · hosted embeds

Embed a tool

Choose a Moon, sky, or mini birth-chart iframe. Set its theme and size, and keep the built-in Zodiacs.org credit.

Planned · no public endpoint

Use hosted computation

A personalized chart API is planned. Its input contract, privacy limits, and release approval remain open.

Run the three examples: local natal chart, personalized transits, and a publisher widget.

Compare support, runtime requirements, and known limits before choosing an integration.

The optional ownership SDK is a separate, read-only integration for registry verification and public ownership reads. Charts, sky data, and widgets do not require it or a wallet.

Shared sky data

The computed dates behind this site's calendars — today's sky, the weeks ahead, retrograde windows, stations, sign ingresses, moon phases, eclipses, and exact aspects — are published as versioned JSON. The files are static, cached at the edge, and open to any origin. There is no key or signup. These files contain no personal birth data: they describe the shared sky, and chart calculation stays on the device.

Quick start
const response = await fetch('https://zodiacs.org/api/v1/sky/today.json', {
  cache: 'no-cache',
  signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000),
});
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Sky request failed: HTTP ${response.status}`);

const sky = await response.json();
if (sky?.schema !== 'zodiacs.sky-api.today.v1'
  || typeof sky.date !== 'string'
  || typeof sky.snapshotAt !== 'string'
  || typeof sky.summary !== 'string'
  || !Array.isArray(sky.bodies)
  || sky.bodies.length === 0
  || sky.bodies.some((body) => !body
    || typeof body !== 'object'
    || typeof body.body !== 'string'
    || typeof body.position !== 'string'
    || typeof body.retrograde !== 'boolean')) {
  throw new Error('Unexpected sky payload');
}

const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
if (sky.date !== today) {
  throw new Error(`Sky edition ${sky.date} is not current (${today} UTC)`);
}
if (sky.snapshotAt !== `${sky.date}T12:00:00.000Z`) {
  throw new Error('Unexpected sky snapshot time');
}

console.log(`Computed positions for ${sky.snapshotAt}`);
console.log(sky.summary);
for (const body of sky.bodies) {
  console.log(body.body, body.position, body.retrograde ? 'Rx' : '');
}


This example checks the payload kind, fields used here, and current UTC edition before displaying its computed snapshot. Keep the snapshot time visible; before noon, it describes positions computed for later that day.

Or from a terminal: curl --fail --silent --show-error https://zodiacs.org/api/v1/sky/today.json

Built for AI agents

Every payload is self-describing. It opens with a summary — one or two plain sentences that state the file's facts, ready to quote — and carries an about block that defines each field and its units, a $schema link to its JSON Schema, and links to the related files. Raw numbers come with formatted twins (lon alongside position, illumination alongside illuminationPercent), and every event carries a label such as "Mercury retrograde in Scorpio, October 24, 2026 – November 13, 2026".

An agent should start at /api/v1/llms.txt: it lists every endpoint, defines every field, states the caveats worth repeating, and maps common questions ("Is Mercury retrograde?", "When is the next full moon?", "When does the Sun enter Libra?") to the file and field that answer them. Tool-calling frameworks can load /api/v1/openapi.json directly, and the daily files have Markdown twins for readers that fetch pages as text.

Daily endpoints
/api/v1/sky/today.json

Today's positions for the Sun, Moon, and eight planets (raw longitudes and formatted labels like 14°53′ Virgo), moon phase and illumination, the active retrograde windows, the next new and full moon with signs and traditional names, the day's exact events, and a plain-language summary. Positions are a 12:00 UTC snapshot. Daily publication is scheduled from 00:00 UTC; check the payload date because delivery can be delayed.

/api/v1/sky/upcoming.json

Every lunation, sign ingress, station, eclipse, and exact aspect in the next 60 days in order, plus the next occurrence of each kind and the current and next Mercury retrograde.

/api/v1/planets/{sun|moon|mercury|venus|mars|jupiter|saturn|uranus|neptune|pluto}.json

One body: position at the daily snapshot, whether it is retrograde, its current and next retrograde window, every window in coverage, and its next sign ingress and station.

/api/v1/signs.json

The twelve signs: element, modality, ruler and traditional ruler, polarity, house, conventional dates, the computed Sun season for this year, and which bodies occupy each sign today.

Yearly endpoints
/api/v1/retrogrades/{2026–2030}.json

Retrograde windows intersecting the year: retrograde and direct station instants and signs, pre- and post-shadow boundaries, duration, and clipping flags where the data boundary truncates a window.

/api/v1/stations/{2026–2030}.json

Every station — a planet turning retrograde or direct — with its sign and degree.

/api/v1/ingresses/{2026–2030}.json

Every planetary sign ingress, with the exact instant and whether the planet entered moving retrograde.

/api/v1/moon-phases/{2026–2030}.json

Every new and full moon with sign, degree, and the traditional full-moon name (Blue for a second full moon in one month).

/api/v1/eclipses/{2026–2030}.json

Solar and lunar eclipses by instant of greatest eclipse: type, kind, sign, obscuration, and totality length.

/api/v1/aspects/{2026–2030}.json

Exact planetary aspects (orb 0) across the year, each with a label such as Mars square Saturn.

Documents and schemas
/api/v1/llms.txt

The guide for AI agents: every endpoint, every field, the caveats worth stating, and which file answers which question.

/api/v1/openapi.json

OpenAPI 3.1 with every JSON Schema embedded, for tool-calling frameworks and typed clients.

/api/v1/schema/{name}.v1.json

Each payload family's JSON Schema (draft 2020-12); every payload links its own under $schema.

/api/v1/sky/today.md and /api/v1/sky/upcoming.md

The daily files rendered as Markdown for readers that fetch pages as text.

/api/v1/index.json

Every endpoint and document above, with coverage and the data vintage.

The contract

Positions are apparent geocentric tropical longitudes from the same engine the calculators use, tested against NASA JPL Horizons reference data. Today's positions are a single snapshot taken at 12:00 UTC (snapshotAt). Publication is scheduled from 00:00 UTC; jobs, deployment, or caches can delay availability. All instants are UTC in ISO 8601, and signs are lowercase slugs with an English signName beside them.

A retrograde window's from and to are its stations unless clippedStart or clippedEnd is true, which means the data boundary truncated the window and the real station lies outside coverage. Within v1, fields are added, never renamed or removed; a breaking change would ship under /api/v2/ and v1 would keep working. Yearly files are byte-stable between data refreshes, so conditional requests are cheap. Year files cover 2026–2030 today and grow as the underlying data is extended; read index.json rather than assuming which years exist.

Freshness and caching

Check the file you consume: date identifies the UTC edition for today's sky, planet files, and signs; snapshotAt is its noon snapshot. Upcoming events use from as the snapshot instant. generatedAt records the file build time and can change without a new edition. The index's coverage.dailyDatedescribes the index; separately cached files can have different dates. Label an older edition by its date or wait for a current one before presenting it as today's sky.

Current cache lifetimes are 300 seconds for sky/today.json, 3,600 seconds for index.json, and 86,400 seconds for the remaining API files, including upcoming events, planets, signs, and Markdown twins. Revalidation can refresh a cached response; always check its edition date as well. Yearly files remain byte-stable between data refreshes.

License and attribution

The data is free to use under CC BY 4.0. Credit "Zodiacs.org" with a link to https://zodiacs.org wherever the data is shown.

Widgets and feeds

If you would rather embed a finished surface than consume JSON, the embeddable widgets render tonight's moon, today's sky, and a mini birth chart inside a sandboxed iframe. Dated editorial is available as RSS: daily horoscopes and the daily sky. The site-wide guide for agents is llms.txt.

Embed today's sky

The same daily edition as /api/v1/sky/today.json, as a finished card: one iframe, no script on your page, and the theme and accent parameters are applied inside the frame. The card links back to zodiacs.org, which is the attribution.
